chapter: Jam sessions, pay and the Vanguard (corrected typing)
title: Sidney Bechet scolds a drummer on playing a chorus
summary: Hodes describes Bechet berating a drummer who took a full chorus and shortened it. He and DeMichael discuss how drummers took breaks and mention Sid Catlett.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Stand in line, just to sit in. And let me tell you something about drummers that you might be surprised to hear. We have a fellow by the name of Kansas [Fields] around Chicago. And he supposedly was a tremendous drummer. Now, in those days, like I say, drums was not breaking it up and all that nonsense. And I'm onstage with Sidney Bechet. And somehow the drummer took the course, and when it got done it wasn't like when we started. We were a little -- the 32 bars were either 30 or 34, something had happened.

And now I'm outside, and Sidney Bechet is eating his rear end out about how to do this, what to do about playing music. Not telling him to hold the sticks or anything, just about the musical part, because drummers then -- there was a
different scene. You got more bars maybe to take a break, but you weren't taking a whole course.
You take certain lengths of time rather than a chorus.
Yeah. And very few people -- now when they give the drummer a course, it seems to me that they just want to rest for a while.
Sid Catlett was the first one that impressed me as being so musical, you could hear the changes in the tune.
